correctionToEarlierPlanning: Twenty is the shipped default, not a universal threshold. Eligibility and provisional fallback must read qc.controlChartMinPoints for the canonical laboratory and method, and freeze that value with the evaluation criteria.
observedPolicyBoundaries: qc.lrmLimitMode already exists: Strict CONTROL_CHART; Basic and Advisory FIXED_WINDOW.
qc.westgardRules already defines reject/warn sets and permits 1-2s, 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s and 10x. Strict currently enables reject 1-3s/2-2s/R-4s and warn 1-2s.
qc.controlChartMinPoints is absent from the current registry and application consumers. Its new shipped default belongs in policyRegistry, with all consumers reading policyService; no inline twenty.
startNativeRun freezes method, policy, reference and rule criteria. A newly approved baseline must be frozen for a new run; existing started runs cannot fetch a newer baseline.

evaluateNativeEvidence currently sees only the current analyte evidence in its run. Cross-run sequence rules need an explicitly frozen history input and deterministic ordering, not an implicit live history query during later evaluation.
NonconformityReport is the existing CRM-failure path. closureTaskService handles sample archive/disposal. Neither is silently repurposed into a generic QC review task.
preparedScientificDesignQuestionsNotYetS: For R-4s, confirm the within-run measurement grouping and whether cross-run pairs are forbidden. For 2-2s/4-1s/10x, confirm the canonical chronology, eligible physical observations and reset at baseline changes.

For baseline proposals, confirm the eligibility of corrected/superseded observations and how outlier flags are recorded. Proposed design retains explicit selected/excluded measurement identities and reasons, refusing ambiguity instead of silently excluding rows.

For enabled 4-1s and 10x rules, confirm scoped QA review-task storage, owner and idempotent evaluation link. Proposed design uses a separate append-only review obligation rather than inventing a CRM nonconformity or sample closure task.

Confirm whether 4-1s and 10x retain the current policy defaults as opt-in permitted rules, or whether a separately reviewed default-policy change is intended. The current reject/warn schema is not silently extended with a new review set.
